classifications.rationale: FocusTrace reports active area elements that omit alt as an HTML content-model warning, but it does not treat aria-label or aria-labelledby as alternative naming mechanisms for that structural check, so the expectations overlap without being equivalent.
FocusTrace checks whether known ARIA states and properties are supported by the resolved role, but its WAI-ARIA 1.3 authoring-warning model and axe applicability/exceptions are not identical.
FocusTrace validates ARIA vocabulary and values but has no rule requiring a non-braille accessible equivalent for braille-specific labels or role descriptions.
FocusTrace deterministically names buttons and links, covering two command-role families, but does not yet provide one equivalent rule for every axe command role such as menuitem variants.
FocusTrace validates known, required and supported ARIA attributes, but it does not yet implement axe's role/state conditional-attribute expectation as a dedicated check.
FocusTrace explicitly reports use of deprecated ARIA roles from its synchronized ARIA registry; this is materially the same authoring expectation.
FocusTrace checks focusable descendants of aria-hidden containers but does not currently prohibit aria-hidden=true on the document body itself.
FocusTrace implements the sequential-focus subset with explicit evidence, while broader focusability/tree edge cases remain outside its current bounded expectation.
FocusTrace checks accessible names for its supported form-field and input-role set, but not every specialized ARIA input applicability path covered by axe.
FocusTrace does not yet have a specialized accessible-name rule for role=meter.
FocusTrace does not yet have a specialized accessible-name rule for role=progressbar.
FocusTrace reports ARIA states/properties prohibited for the resolved role, but it uses the current ARIA authoring registry and warning semantics rather than axe's exact rule contract.
FocusTrace checks required states/properties for resolved ARIA roles; registry version, implicit-role handling and outcome semantics differ from axe.
FocusTrace validates whether semantic children are allowed by supported ARIA container roles, but it does not yet verify that required owned child roles are present.
FocusTrace checks required accessibility parent context, but its current ARIA model and repair/ownership boundaries are not asserted to be identical to axe.
